title: Contact field normalization scrapbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for weird contact-field examples we keep hitting in the user corpus. Focus: phone numbers, emails, compact contact blobs (user-submitted 'contact' fields), and small heuristics for automated normalization vs. manual triage. Not a canonical spec — draft for discussion and sampling experiments.

High-level goals:
- Increase automated normalization coverage without inflating false positives in labeled datasets.
- Surface ambiguous examples to human review with deterministic flags.
- Keep canonicalization reversible-ish where useful (store raw + canonical).

Common patterns and oddballs (examples pulled from logs):
1) Phone numbers
   - Local-ish: "(415) 555-0132" -> easy to parse.
   - Compressed: "+14155550132" -> E.164 candidate.
   - With extension: "212-555-0000 x123" / "+44 20 7946 0958 ext 42" -> preserve extension token separate field.
   - Embedded words: "call me at five five five - oh-one-two" -> needs ASR/word2digit pipeline or mark as 'verbalized' for review.
   - Fragmented across fields: name line contains phone, address second line contains phone again -> dedupe logic by normalizing and comparing.
   - Numbers with letters: "1-800-FLOWERS" -> map letters to digits if labeler config says so, otherwise mark as 'alpha-phone'.
   - Leading zeros/IDD: "0011 61 2 9876 5432" (Australia via AUS IDD) -> try to canonicalize via libphonenumber but watch for stray leading 00 used locally.
   - Noisy punctuation: "+1 (415)#555*0132" -> strip non-numeric except leading plus and record original.

2) Emails and obfuscation
   - Straightforward: "j.smith@example.com" -> canonical lowercased.
   - Obfuscated: "jane [at] example[dot]com" or "jane(at)example dot com" -> convert common obfuscations for contact extraction pipeline, but keep original and mark 'deobfuscated' flag.
   - Spaces/newlines in domain: "foo@exam ple.com" -> suspicious: sometimes user-entered typos; try auto-fix only if domain TLD is valid and mx lookup ok.
   - Unicode homoglyphs: "аpple@exаmple.com" where Cyrillic a used -> normalizer should run unicode-normalize + homoglyph map for latin subset. If mapping ambiguous, surface for manual.
   - Role addresses: "support+billing@example.com" -> preserve plus-tagging.

3) Compact contact blobs (single freeform 'contact' field)
   - Examples: "John Doe, 415-555-0123 / jdoe@corp.com / SF" or "Call: +44 7911 123456; Email - bsmith at email dot co uk"
   - Strategy: run multi-pass extraction: emails -> phones -> social handles -> residual text. If multiple entities found, emit list. Keep ordering and raw offsets for provenance.

4) Social handles / non-standard IDs
   - Twitter: "@janesmith"; Instagram: "instagram.com/jane.s"; Slack handle: "@jane:acme.slack.com" -> treat as identifier type separate from email/phone.
   - Some entries contain non-US formats like WeChat IDs and QQ numbers: classify as 'social' and add sub-type when pattern matches.

5) PII noise in remarks
   - Sentences: "Do not call after 9pm. If emergency: 415 555 6666" -> labeler should extract the number but also preserve context note ("do_not_call_after_21:00") as metadata if present. Could be useful for downstream ops.

Edgecase heuristics (rules-of-thumb)
- Confidence tiers: auto-normalize if libphonenumber or regex-plus-domain-check returns high-confidence. Otherwise tag 'low_conf' and route to small review queue.
- Minimal mutation principle: store raw_text, canonical_value, normalizer_notes. Avoid destructive overwrites.
- Priority order when fields conflict: explicit email in 'email' column > email extracted from freeform > match in address line. But record provenance.
- When two phones match after canonicalization, keep single canonical + list of raw variants.
- If phone has letters and maps to valid toll-free format, add 'alpha_converted' flag; otherwise surface.

Annotation guidance (for labelers)
- Label 'PHONE' span should include all digits and extension tokens (x, ext, #) contiguous to the number. Ex: "(415) 555-0132 x21" -> single PHONE span including "x21".
- Label 'EMAIL' span should include plus-tags and subaddressing. Do not attempt to split username and domain (unless asked).
- For obfuscated emails, label both the raw span and add a canonical_email attribute in the label UI (manual entry) when straightforward. If labeler cannot confidently deobfuscate, mark as 'OBFUSCATED_EMAIL'.
- For multi-contact blobs, annotate each entity separately with offsets. If the UI doesn't support offsets, paste CSV of extracted entities into comments.

Sampling & QA
- Create a targeted sample of low_conf examples: all entries where normalizer returns 'score < 0.7' OR contains non-ASCII letters in domain OR contains alphabetic chars in numeric spans. Aim for 1k samples per month for labeler review.
- Periodic paired-review: 5% of items flagged as auto-normalized get adjudicated by pair review to measure false-normalize rate.
- Track metrics: normalize_coverage (percent of contact fields with canonical value), false_normalize_rate, manual_review_backlog, avg_time_to_adjudicate.

Regular expressions / quick parser notes (for experiments only)
- Loose phone finder: (?:\+?\d{1,3}[\s\-\.\(\)]*)?(?:\d{1,4}[\s\-\.\(\)]*){2,}\b  -- prototype; will catch a lot of false positives; chain with libphonenumber parse.
- Obfuscated email hints: patterns for "\[at\]", "\(at\)", " at ", and common dot substitutes (" dot ", "[dot]"). Use word-boundary checks to avoid misfires.

Open questions / items to try
- How often do we see non-E.164 canonical numbers that nevertheless map to valid local numbers? Do we need a locale inference pass before normalizing?
- Should we attempt automated letter->digit conversion (1-800-FLOWERS) for downstream routing? Risk: false mapping for random alpha strings.
- Is preservation of contextual instructions ("do not call after 9pm") valuable enough to add small structured flags? Might help CS workflows.
- How to handle contact fields with multiple contacts belonging to different people in same blob? (e.g., "Primary: John 415... Secondary: Lisa 415...") – prefer multi-entity extraction and label as contacts[0], contacts[1].

Implementation notes for pipeline work (for infra handoff)
- Keep extractor as stateless microservice: input raw string, return list of {type, raw_span, canonical_value?, confidence, normalized_tokens, provenance_id}. If no canonical_value, field empty.
- Rate-limit aggressive deobfuscation heuristics to avoid noisy mass changes; go gradual by experimenting on 1% of traffic with logging.
- Add a small 'review microqueue' service that stores low_conf items and exposes simple accept/reject toggles for labelers.

Quick manual checks (scratch checklist)
- [ ] Pull 500 most recent "contact" freeform fields, run extractor, measure fraction with >1 entity.
- [ ] Build sample set of obfuscated emails found last 30 days, categorize obfuscation types.
- [ ] Measure how many phone numbers fail libphonenumber parse but contain 7+ digits (likely local formats).
- [ ] Mock UI snippet for labelers showing raw_text + suggested canonical + one-click accept/edit.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc ephemeral. Move to shared Confluence when we have consensus — but keep example corpus excerpts in a separate file with redactions.
- Discuss with legal before adding any automated canonicalization that could trigger PDPA/CCPA concerns (we're storing raw + canonical, but storing canonical might change retention needs).

Random example bank (for unit tests)
- "mike AT example DOT com" -> canonical: mike@example.com, flagged deobfuscated.
- "+1-800-FLOWERS" -> "+1-800-356-9377" if we choose conversion, else tag.
- "тест@пример.рф" -> non-latin domain; preserve raw and attempt IDN punycode if requested.
- "Call (numbers): 555-1234 / 555-2345 ext2" -> two PHONE entities, second with extension.

If you pick this up, first small deliverable: sample 1k recent freeform contact rows, run current extractor, and attach failure examples to JIRA-ENG-9876.

-- Maya

(End of scratchpad)
